mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS (monetary easing) signals lower interest rates, boosting equity valuations and leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window, or 20-day returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent low UNRATE (labor cost suppression) reduces inflationary pressures, fostering investor confidence and positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises above 6% in the next 60 days, leading to negative returns despite initial low rates.

mechanism_narrative: An upward surge in INDPRO (supply growth) indicates robust production capacity, driving short-term positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines below its 2010-04-01 level, negating the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in FEDFUNDS above 2% triggers monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains above 2% for 30 days without negative returns, or returns turn positive despite the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: GDPC1 crossing above 12,000 (quarterly billings) signals robust demand, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDPC1 reverts below 12,000 within 20 days, failing to sustain positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE surpassing 6% signals rising labor costs, leading to inflation concerns and negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 6% for 60 days without negative returns, or returns turn positive during the regime.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS (<2%) and UNRATE (<6%) creates a dual easing environment, amplifying positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Either FEDFUNDS or UNRATE breaches the threshold, negating the combined signal.

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 3%), 60-day S&P 500 returns are consistently negative due to higher interest rates.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS reverts below 3% within 60 days without negative returns, or returns turn positive during the regime.
